answers.docs.gaps:
(a) JSON key order. templating.md, "Structured Output": "| `Json` | `serde_json::to_string_pretty(data)` |".
If that were literally the handler struct, key order would be declaration order.
`InstallView` is declared `{ installed, count }`, and `pnpmlike install --output json`
produced:

    {"count":2,"installed":[{"name":"alpha","version":"1.0.0"},...]}

Keys alphabetized, so the data goes through a sorted map on the way. Nothing in docs/
mentions that, and it matters to any spec that pins the bytes of its machine document.

(b) The post-output example is wrong — quoted under question 4(a).

(c) `TextOutput` and `ArtifactOutput` are named in execution-model.md and nowhere
described. `TextOutput` turns out to have public `formatted` and `raw` fields; which
one the final write uses, and what `raw` is for, is not written down anywhere I could
find.

(d) Returning `RenderedOutput::Silent` from a post-output hook is undocumented.
execution-model.md says a post-output hook "Can transform the final string" and lists
`Silent` only as an input variant. Returning it does suppress the write entirely — I
verified `pnpmlike list` in an empty workspace emits zero bytes on stdout — but that
is behaviour I had to discover, and it is the only way to get "prints nothing at all"
past "`App::run` writes a handled command's text with `writeln!`" (templating.md,
"The Trailing-Newline Contract").

(e) app-configuration.md shows `.hooks("db.migrate", Hooks::new()...)` without saying
whether it returns `Self` or `Result<Self, _>`, in a snippet where the neighbouring
`.command_with(...)?` does carry a `?`. It returns `Self`.
answers.friction:
(a) The post-output hook example does not compile. execution-model.md line 174:

    Ok(RenderedOutput::Text(format!("{}\n-- Generated by MyApp", s)))

    error[E0277]: the trait bound `TextOutput: From<std::string::String>` is not satisfied
    error[E0599]: the method `to_string` exists for reference `&TextOutput`, but its
      trait bounds were not satisfied
      doesn't satisfy `TextOutput: ToString` or `TextOutput: std::fmt::Display`

`RenderedOutput::Text` carries a `TextOutput { formatted, raw }`, and nothing in
docs/ says so. This cost the compiler-probe described in question 3.

(b) The reporter has to know the output mode, and a handler is not allowed to.
output-modes.md, "Keep Output Mode Out of Handlers": "Output mode is a rendering
concern and is deliberately absent from `CommandContext`." That is the right rule for
*stdout*, but SPEC.md's reporter table has a row keyed on it — "the output mode is a
machine mode (`json`, `yaml`, `xml`, `csv`) → `ndjson`" — and the reporter is a
*stderr* concern. There is no seam for "a non-rendering subsystem needs to know what
stdout is carrying", so I scan argv for `--output` at startup.

(c) Neither stderr channel exists in the framework. `grep -rn
"reporter\|progress\|loglevel\|quiet\|verbose" docs/` returns only clap-flag examples
and two notes saying the *test harness* cannot simulate progress bars
("If your CLI drives progress bars, raw-mode TUIs, ... the harness can't simulate
that"). Both channels are hand-rolled onto stderr from inside the handlers, which
sits awkwardly against error-handling.md's "Do not print or call `process::exit` from
handlers" — a rule written about stdout, with no stated carve-out for a second stderr
channel.

(d) The one registration shape that *is* sanctioned for writing your own bytes costs
too much. passthrough.md: "No structured output modes ... a passthrough handler never
produces an `Output` value, so those modes have nothing to act on." `run` is exactly
its use case ("run this external process and let it own the terminal"), but SPEC.md
also wants `run`'s exit status propagated verbatim, and the documented seam for that
(`ExternalFailure`) is described only through `HandlerResult`. I used a normal handler
returning `Output::Silent` instead, which gives both.

answers.summary:
`pnpmlike`, complete and building clean, in `app/`. `cargo build` succeeds with no
warnings from my code; `cargo test` runs 24 unit tests and 25 black-box integration
tests (`app/tests/cli.rs`, which spawns the real binary in a per-test sandbox
directory and asserts exact stdout bytes, exact stderr bytes and exit status), all
passing.

Layout: `manifest.rs` is the CLI-free core (line-oriented parsing, located errors,
missing file = empty workspace). `channels.rs` owns the two stderr channels — the
four reporter forms and the three log levels. `session.rs` resolves one invocation
(which manifest, which reporter, which level), with `auto`'s resolution table taking
stderr attendance as a parameter so it is testable without a terminal. `cli.rs` is
the clap surface (all pnpmlike flags global, so `run --manifest x` reads like
`list --manifest x`). `handlers.rs` are the Standout adapters; `views.rs` the
serializable view data; `hooks.rs` a post-output hook that shapes the stdout
document. Commands are registered with `#[derive(Dispatch)]`; `run` is
`#[dispatch(pure, silent)]` so it has no template and nothing renders over the
child's bytes.

Verified against the spec's five stressed interactions: reporter resolution keys off
stderr, not stdout; a machine output mode keeps stdout to exactly one document and
switches `auto` to `ndjson`; `-q`, `--reporter silent` and `--silent` reach the two
channels independently; a child's stdout, stderr and exit status pass through
unaltered in every output mode; and the four no-answer paths stay distinct (absent
manifest 0, malformed manifest 1, bad flag value 2, unknown script 3).

Three residual uncertainties, all narrow. (a) The spec says the `ndjson` `done` entry
comes "after the last step of a successful `install`"; an empty workspace has no last
step. I emit `{"event":"done","installed":0}` anyway, reading `done` as terminal for
every successful install — the "writes nothing at all" carve-out is stated only for
the `default` reporter. (b) No pty is available in this sandbox (`openpty: Operation
not permitted`), so the "stderr is an attended terminal → `default`" row is covered by
unit test rather than end to end; only the `std::io::stderr().is_terminal()` call
itself is unexercised. (c) The summary is always "packages" — the spec gives
`2 packages installed.` and `0 packages installed.` and no singular form.
answers.workarounds:
(a) `session.rs`, `Invocation::from_argv` — an argv scan for `--output` / `--output=`,
stopping at the first bare `--` and skipping the values of value-taking flags. It
exists only to answer "is stdout carrying a machine document", for the reporter's
`auto` row. See friction (b). It is handed to handlers as app state rather than
recomputed, so there is one place to delete when a seam exists.

(b) `hooks.rs`, `shape_document` — a post-output hook doing three things the render
pass will not: turning an empty render into `RenderedOutput::Silent` (so an empty
workspace's `list` prints zero bytes instead of `writeln!`'s newline), collapsing the
pretty-printed JSON onto one line, and re-emitting the top-level keys in the order
SPEC.md spells them. It guards on "parses as a JSON object", so text, YAML, XML and
CSV renderings pass through untouched. Undoing the framework's own serialization
formatting from a hook is a workaround, not a design.

(c) `handlers.rs` — `ExternalFailure` carries the manifest error (status 1) and the
unknown script (status 3), not only the genuinely external child status.
error-handling.md says "Use `ExternalFailure` only when another operation owns the
status and diagnostic contract", so this is off-label: an ordinary handler error would
give the right status for the manifest case but would re-frame the message as
`Error: {error}`, and there is no seam at all for exit 3. `ExternalFailure` is the only
one that yields both an exact status and a verbatim stderr spelling, which is what the
spec pins.

(d) `handlers.rs` — the failing-script `ExternalFailure` carries an empty diagnostic.
SPEC.md leaves what pnpmlike says about a failing script unspecified, and an empty
payload is the smallest thing that can be appended after the child's own stderr.

(e) `channels.rs` writes both stderr channels directly with `write_all`, from inside
handlers. See friction (c).
